summary: Many reviewers get strong value from the travel credit, lounges, insurance, points boost and transfer partners, often more than the annual fee. The most common complaints are credits that are hard to use (DoorDash, The Edit, StubHub), poor support when portal bookings go wrong, crowded lounges, and a higher fee after the refresh.

Many reviewers say it changed how they handle money, with zero-based budgeting that is worth the subscription once learned. The main complaint is price increases, and quite a few moved to Actual Budget or spreadsheets. Others cite manual entry, a learning curve, bank sync gaps, and interface changes.

Reviewers who travel or live in cities say the lounges, Fine Hotels stays and credits (Uber, Resy, airline, Lululemon) outweigh the high annual fee. Others call it a coupon book that is hard to use and poor for everyday earning. Lounge crowding and recent hotel credit changes bothered some.

Most reviewers rate the customer service highly and like having investing, cash and retirement accounts in one place, with the cash sweep earning interest. Many prefer it to Vanguard and Schwab. A sizable minority report transfers or deposits held for weeks, account locks, and a glitchy app.

Reviewers like the interface, reporting and Mint-style overview, and many moved from Mint, YNAB or Copilot. The most common complaints are accounts that stop syncing and slow support, plus higher pricing and budgeting that some find less hands-on than YNAB. Experience depends on the banks connected.

Many reviewers like it for travel, currency exchange, transfers and the app, and some use it as a main bank for years. The dominant complaint is support: accounts frozen, blocked or closed with little explanation, slow appeals and chat bots. Outages and fee changes also came up, so some keep another bank as backup.

Reviewers like earning points on rent with no annual fee, plus the transfer partners and travel perks. Many are unhappy with the 2.0 changes, which they say cut benefits and made earning more complicated. Support experiences are mixed, with several fraud cases handled well and others slowly.

Most reviewers use it for international transfers and like the low, upfront fees, good exchange rates and reliability, including for large sums. The main complaints are accounts blocked or transfers held, cancelled or delayed during reviews, with support hard to reach. A few found bank wires cheaper for very large amounts.

Most reviewers are long-time customers who like the app, buckets, lack of fees and ATM fee reimbursement, and many praise the customer service. Some report accounts locked or frozen with slow, frustrating support. A few found rates lower than competitors or missed having cash deposits and branches.

Most reviewers describe a simple high-yield savings account with quick transfers, no fees and no problems for years. The main complaint is accounts locked or withdrawals blocked after security or identity reviews, with frustrating phone support. Some also mention rates falling and the lack of a mobile app.

Most reviewers who eat out and buy groceries a lot are happy with the 4x earning and points value. The annual fee is the main sticking point, and the dining and delivery credits (Dunkin, Grubhub, Resy) are easy for city dwellers but awkward elsewhere. Some cancel or keep it only after retention offers.

Reviewers mostly love the high cash back on dining, entertainment, groceries and streaming, and it is often a most-used card, sometimes paired with the Venture X. The annual fee is worth it for heavy dining and entertainment spenders but not for everyone. A few report accounts closed or restricted without explanation.

Reviewers who like it praise the clean, fast interface, quick transaction syncing and good recurring and investment views. Complaints are slow development, thin reports and budgeting, and the lack of a web or Android app. Some left for Monarch or YNAB, while others stay because of the design.

Reviewers mostly find it easy to justify, as the travel credit and anniversary miles offset the annual fee, and they value the lounge access, simple 2x earning and portal pricing. Downsides are a portal-only travel credit that some find cumbersome and recent lounge access changes that hurt solo travelers and those with guests.

Reviewers value the Hyatt and airline transfer partners, primary rental car coverage and no foreign transaction fees, with the points often worth it for travel. The main frustrations are a portal hotel credit that is hard to use, reduced redemption value, and the annual fee. Support experiences are mixed.

Most reviewers like the clean app, daily cash back, extra cash back on Apple Pay and no foreign transaction fees, and many use it mainly for interest-free Apple device financing. The physical card earns less, and some find it thin on benefits. Fraud and dispute handling through Goldman Sachs frustrated a number of reviewers.

Most reviewers use it as a simple flat-rate catch-all and keep it for years, with easy redemption and handy price protections. The main complaint is Citi customer service, especially fraud flags and disputes ruled for the merchant. Some also dislike benefits being cut, the shift to ThankYou points, and the foreign transaction fee.

Reviewers mostly like it as a simple flat-rate catch-all with a solid sign-up bonus, no annual fee and cell phone protection. Product changes from other Wells Fargo cards were easy. Complaints include redemption rules, such as increments and the removed check option, low credit limits and weaker customer service for some.

Most reviewers use it as an everyday catch-all, earning a flat rate plus bonus rewards on dining and drugstores, often alongside a Sapphire card. Product changes and in-branch offers usually went smoothly. Some say it feels less competitive now, and a few had promotions or bonus credits not honored or missing.

Reviewers mostly like the rotating bonus categories, the dining and drugstore bonus, and stacking offers such as PayPal quarters for much higher returns. Some find the categories a hassle to track or unhelpful in certain quarters. A few had trouble getting welcome bonuses honored. Phone protection claims were generally easy.
